section_1.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
section_1.content: Define the distinction between Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) and PDEs. Use a 2D animation: an ODE represents a point moving along a line (time-dependent), while a PDE represents a surface (like a vibrating drumhead) changing over time and space.
section_1.example: Compare a single pendulum (ODE) to the ripples on a pond caused by a stone (PDE).

section_2.title: The Core Anatomy: Variables and Operators
section_2.content: Introduce the notation: u(x, y, t). Explain partial derivatives (∂) as 'slopes in specific directions.' Use a 3D wireframe grid: showing how a surface bends along the X-axis vs. the Y-axis.
section_2.example: Visualize a heat map on a metal plate: how the temperature gradient (∂u/∂x) moves from a hot burner toward the cool edges.

section_3.title: The Heat Equation: A Practical Foundation
section_3.content: Introduce the Heat Equation: ∂u/∂t = α∇²u. Explain ∇² (the Laplacian) as the difference between the temperature at a point and its average neighbors. Animation: A cluster of heat particles diffusing from a dense center to empty space.
section_3.example: A cat sleeping on a cold floor: the heat equation models how the floor warms up under the cat over time.

section_4.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions
section_4.content: Explain that a PDE needs 'rules' to have a unique solution. Use the analogy of a guitar string: the length of the string (boundary) and how you pluck it (initial state) determine the sound.
section_4.example: Simulating a character's cape in a video game: the fixed points at the shoulders are the boundary conditions.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_5.content: Recap that PDEs describe how things change in space and time. Connect to modern applications: Fluid dynamics, quantum mechanics, and artificial intelligence models.
section_5.example: Display a montage of a weather simulation, a bridge under wind stress, and the cooling of a computer processor.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
